newsitem.title: USA: Olin sets spin-off, sale of businesses.
newsitem.headline: Olin sets spin-off, sale of businesses.

text.p: Olin Corp. said Thursday it will spin off to shareholders its defence and aerospace divisions as a new business and sell certain chemical operations as part of a restructuring to narrow the company's focus.
Olin said it will use part of the proceeds from the divestitures to repurchase up to 10 percent of its outstanding shares and will split its common stock on a two-for-one basis.
Stockholders will receive new shares in the spun off defence and aerospace company, which will be named Primex Technologies, Inc. Olin said last November that it was considering such a spinoff.

Olin said it also will sell chemical operations involved in producing resins and adhesives at Lake Charles, La., to ARCO Chemical Company for $565 million in cash and will seek a buyer for its polyol, glycol and surfactants businesses at its Doe Run facility at Brandenburg, Ky.
Each Olin shareholder will receive one Primex share for every 10 post-split shares of Olin. The transaction is expected to be completed around the end of this year.
In response to the news, Olin shares shot $4.375 higher to close at $88.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Don Pattison said overall the moves will result in a win for Olin shareholders. He said the expected yield on the Primex shares will result in a larger payout than before the spinoff.
"If they keep the Primex stock, they will be getting a higher yield in total than before, and Primex will have some sort of value, it will be a piece of paper they can sell," Pattison said.

Pattison praised the company's decision to sell chemical units. "Getting rid of the urethanes, the foam you see in cars and bedding, at Lake Charles makes sense because it is a cyclical business at the peak of its earnings cycle," he said. He added that the isocyanates business, which makes water-based paints for cars that cut emissions, was overdue and "has been a drag on earnings."
The Olin divisions being spun off employ about 2,600 people and had total sales in 1995 of about $500 million, Olin said.
James G. Hascall, an Olin executive vice president whose current operating responsibilities include the two divisions, will become chairman and chief executive officer of Primex.
Primex will be headquartered in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Olin's Winchester ammunition division will not be part of the spin-off.
Norwalk, Conn.-based Olin produces chemicals, metals, microelectronic materials, sporting and military ammunition and aerospace products.
The company employs about 13,000 people. It had 1995 sales of $3.2 billion.
